alerts.channels_config: Channels are set in .env — email (SMTP), ntfy, Telegram, webhook, Apprise. Restart to apply changes.
alerts.channels_none: No channels configured — nothing will be sent
alerts.channels_recommended: Best pairing: ntfy for the fastest phone push — install the app, subscribe to your topic — plus email as a written record.
alerts.how_intrusion: Intrusion signals — a door, window, trunk, or frunk opening, an unlock, or the vehicle moving with no one inside — come straight from vehicle state changes, so they're reliable.
alerts.how_polled: Standard Sentry Mode triggers (someone approaches, the vehicle starts recording) are detected from center_display_state=7 — that value means Sentry Mode has been triggered and the touchscreen is showing the recording warning, not that Sentry Mode is simply on. No setup needed, but while parked your vehicle is polled every 30 seconds, so short events can be missed. For real-time detection with no gaps, connect Fleet Telemetry (see the docs).
alerts.how_sessions: Back-to-back activity merges into one session ({dedup}-second window). Anything lasting more than {escalate} seconds, or a second trigger soon after, escalates to high priority — so one busy night doesn't bury you in alerts.
alerts.no_sentry: No Sentry Mode activity yet. Once the vehicle is parked with Sentry Mode on, anyone who approaches shows up here.
alerts.policies_help: People walk past your own driveway all day — no need to hear about every one. Locations come from your saved places in Settings.
alerts.policies_intrusion_note: Intrusion alerts — door opened, vehicle unlocked — ignore this setting and are always sent.
alerts.polled_off: Polled detection is off in .env (SENTRY_POLLED_ALERTS=false). Only Fleet Telemetry and intrusion signals will alert.
alerts.test_failed: Not sent. Check the channel settings in .env
alerts.title: Sentry Mode & alerts
auto.help: Do something automatically when an event happens. New rules start disabled — they can operate your car, so look them over before switching them on. Unlocking the doors is not in the command list by default.
auto.save_note: Saved rules stay disabled; turn them on with the switch in the list.
auto.title: Automations

body.idle_fee: Unplug soon — Superchargers charge by the minute once charging finishes.
cmd.error.asleep: Vehicle asleep or offline (408). Run Wake vehicle, then retry.
cmd.error.missing_param: This command needs a value for “{param}”.
cmd.error.no_eid: No Tesla vehicle ID (eid) on record for this vehicle.
cmd.error.no_location: Window control needs the vehicle's current location, and none is on record yet. Drive or wake the vehicle, then retry.
cmd.error.no_token: No Tesla API token. Connect your Tesla on the setup page, or paste an access token in Settings.
cmd.error.no_vin: No VIN on record for this vehicle. The Fleet API and the signing proxy address vehicles by VIN.
cmd.error.token_expired: Token expired (401). It refreshes on its own — retry in a minute.
cmdk.a_no_data: No data yet. It appears once the vehicle reports.
cmdk.empty: No matches. Try a command or page name.
cmdk.needs_value: Type a number first, e.g. “80” for 80{unit}.
cmdk.title: Search
dashcam.empty.encryption: Clips import but won't play? Check Controls › Safety › Dashcam Encryption on the touchscreen: encrypted clips can't be read directly.
dashcam.empty.setup: Or copy the TeslaCam folder from the drive into data/teslacam/ on this machine, then rescan.
dashcam.empty.title: No clips yet
dashcam.empty.usb_cta: Open clips from a USB drive →
dashcam.empty.usb_why: Tesla never uploads dashcam footage; it lives only on the USB drive in your vehicle. Plug the drive into this computer and the USB page reads it in place: clips play in your browser, and nothing is copied or uploaded. Import only the events you want to keep.
dashcam.hevc_note: {n} clips use HEVC and are transcoded for playback; the first play takes a moment.
dashcam.locked_body: The files are there and the timeline is right, but nothing can be read out of them — this is what encrypted footage looks like. Tesla can encrypt dashcam and Sentry Mode recordings on the drive; turn it off on the touchscreen under Controls → Safety → Dashcam Encryption, then record again. Clips saved while it was on stay unreadable. A partial copy off the drive looks the same way, so it's worth re-copying first.
dashcam.sei.none: No driving data (older software, parked clip, or encrypted)
dashcam.sei.title: Segment SEI stats
dashcam.title: Dashcam
drives.pick_hint: Select a drive to see its route
drives.track_none: No route data for this drive
energy.baseline_note: Leave blank to use the best range ever observed. If you installed OhmyTesla years after buying the car, that best-ever figure already includes the degradation — enter the original EPA/WLTP range to measure it properly.
energy.eff_sub: What cold weather actually costs you
energy.no_history_sub: Charging sessions and drives appear here as they happen. Data starts from the day you connected your account — Tesla's API doesn't provide history.
energy.no_rates: Rates not set — costs can't be calculated
energy.range_efficiency_sub: distance driven vs rated range used
energy.soc_exposure: Time spent at each charge level
energy.soc_note: {pct}% of parked time above 80%. Sitting at a high charge level is a known cause of calendar ageing — charge to 100% before long trips, not overnight every night.
energy.soc_note_lfp: This is an LFP pack — Tesla recommends charging it to 100% regularly, so high charge levels are not a concern here.
energy.use_sub: Added at the plug, by month
energy.vampire_note: Measured between consecutive drives with no charging in between. Sentry Mode is the usual cause — it draws 150–300 W continuously.
fsd.cta_body: Every dashcam frame carries speed, steering angle and Autopilot state (driving clips on software 2025.44.25+). Index once to see Autopilot share, disengagements and hard-braking spots, with no API fees.
fsd.encrypted: {n} clips are encrypted (default since software 2026.20). Turn encryption off on the touchscreen under Controls › Safety to make new clips readable; existing ones need decrypting with your Tesla account.
fsd.no_sei: Indexed {n} clips, but none carry driving data. Parked Sentry clips and driving clips from before software 2025.44.25 don't have it.
fsd.note: From {clips} indexed clips (~{secs} min) · {nosei} without driving data
fsd.title: Driving analysis
fsd.unreadable: {n} clips can't be read. Usually the files are incomplete (the USB drive was pulled mid-write) or encrypted (default since software 2026.20; turn it off in Controls › Safety).
insights.chart.range_sub: Monthly rated range scaled to a full charge — the clearest read on capacity loss
insights.chart.temp_sub: What cold weather actually costs you
insights.tariff_hint: Set your electricity rates in Settings to see charging costs. Time-of-use plans work too.

player.meta.title: Clip details

rule.sentry_frunk_opened: Frunk opened while Sentry Mode was on

security.clear_confirm: Delete every alert in the history? Sentry Mode activity and the alerts themselves are unaffected.
security.email_missing_password: SMTP_HOST is set but SMTP_PASS is empty, so nothing can be sent. Gmail needs an App Password (not your login password) — generate one at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords, put it in .env, then run ./omt restart.
security.email_missing_to: SMTP_HOST is set but SMTP_TO is empty — there is nobody to send to.
security.email_missing_user: SMTP_HOST is set but SMTP_USER is empty. Fill in the account that sends the mail, then run ./omt restart.
security.no_channels_body: Sentry Mode is being watched, but no notification channel is set up — nothing will reach you. Add one and this vanishes.
security.snoozed: Muted for {n} more min — intrusion alerts still get through.
security.snoozed_all: Everything muted for {n} more min, including intrusion alerts.
sentry.policy.escalated: Push only if it repeats or lasts
session.reason_repeat: Triggered again right after the last event
session.source_polled: Polled every 30 seconds — short events can be missed
session.title_triggered: Sentry Mode: someone near your vehicle
settings.about.heading: About
settings.about.line1: OhmyTesla — a self-hosted Tesla companion. AGPL-⁠3.0.
settings.about.line2: Not affiliated with the TeslaMate project or Tesla, Inc.
settings.about.line3: Everything else — notification channels, TeslaCam folder, portal password, map tiles — lives in .env at the project root. Run docker compose up -d after editing.
settings.abrp_off: ABRP relay is off. Set ABRP_ENABLED and ABRP_TOKEN in .env to send live data to A Better Routeplanner.
settings.bridge.enable_ok: SentryMode streaming on for {configured} vehicles. Takes effect the next time each one connects.
settings.bridge.heading: Live Sentry stream (hosted relay)
settings.bridge.help_experimental: This relay's protocol hasn't been verified against a live account. If no events arrive, adjust the FLEET_BRIDGE_* settings against docs/FLEET-TELEMETRY.md.
settings.bridge.help_verified: Leave SENTRY_POLLED_ALERTS=true: polling stands down while the stream is live and takes back over if the relay fails or runs out of quota.
settings.bridge.intro: By default, Sentry alerts are inferred from polling, so brief events can slip past. A hosted relay streams Tesla's live state instead (Aware = someone close, Panic = alarm), within seconds and without misses. No public IP needed: the hub connects outbound.
settings.bridge.no_events: Connected, but no events yet. The relay probably isn't sending the SentryMode field; use the button below.
settings.bridge.no_vehicles: Not connected: no vehicle VIN yet. Connect your Tesla account and it syncs automatically.
settings.bridge.off_help:
To enable, set these in .env at the project root:
FLEET_BRIDGE_ENABLED=true
FLEET_BRIDGE_PROVIDER=teslemetry
FLEET_BRIDGE_TOKEN=your-token
then run docker compose up -d. See docs/FLEET-TELEMETRY.md.
settings.car_saved_restart: Saved. Run ./omt restart to apply; TeslaMate caches these until it restarts.
settings.channels_note: Email, ntfy, Telegram, webhook and Apprise are configured in .env — restart to apply.
settings.data_export_help: Everything, in open formats other tools can read.
settings.data_ok_long: No gaps or missing records found in the last 90 days.
settings.detect_none: Couldn't detect a region. Connecting your Tesla account helps.
settings.env_note: Notification channels, the dashcam folder, the portal password and map tiles live in .env. Run ./omt restart after editing.
settings.ice_help: Enter a comparable gas car's consumption and your fuel price. Leave blank to hide the comparison.
settings.issue_charges_without_cost: Charging sessions without cost: {n}. Set your rates, then Recompute.
settings.issue_drives_without_track: Drives without a route: {n}. Their maps will be empty.
settings.issue_gaps: Gaps with no data: {n}. Data collection was probably down.
settings.issue_missing_addresses: Drive endpoints without an address: {n} (address lookup failed or timed out).
settings.maint_help: Tesla has no fixed service schedule, but tire rotation, filters and brake fluid still go by distance or time. Marking an item done restarts it from today.
settings.mcp_hint: Ask an AI assistant about your vehicle: claude mcp add --transport http ohmytesla http://localhost:8800/mcp
settings.places_confirm: Remove this place? Past drives and charging sessions are unaffected.
settings.places_filled: Filled in from the vehicle's location.
settings.places_note: Name the places you park often. Charging costs, Sentry alerts and drive endpoints show these names instead of addresses.
settings.push.heading: Notifications
settings.push.insecure_origin:
Browsers disable Web Push on insecure origins like {origin}.
Open it at http://localhost:8800, or put the portal behind HTTPS (e.g. Tailscale) for a trusted certificate. ntfy, Telegram and email are unaffected.
settings.push.intro: Native browser push, no third-party account. On iPhone, first add this page to your Home Screen (iOS 16.4+). Android and desktop Chrome work as is.
settings.push.need_permission: Push needs notification permission. If no prompt appeared, check this site's notification settings in your browser.
settings.push.unsupported: This browser doesn't support push. On iPhone, add this page to your Home Screen and open it from there.
settings.sleep_note: These control how long logging waits before letting the vehicle sleep. Longer waits capture more detail; shorter waits save battery.
settings.speed_limit_help: Useful when someone else is driving. Leave blank to turn it off.
settings.tariff.dirty: Rates changed. Recompute to update past costs.
settings.tariff.heading: Electricity rates
settings.tariff.intro: Set your rates once and every charging session is priced automatically, time-of-use included.
settings.tariff.loc_note: Places come from your saved places. Home is often time-of-use; work may be free.
settings.tariff.saved: Saved. Recompute to update past costs.
settings.tariff.template_applied: Template applied. Enter your rates and save.
settings.tariff.template_note: Fills in time periods only; you enter the rates
settings.tariff.unconfigured: Rates are all zero. Set them first; nothing was saved.
settings.tariff.uncovered: · {uncovered_sessions} sessions ran outside your rate periods
settings.tariff.warn_bad_period: {scope}: period “{period}” has an invalid start or end time.
settings.tariff.warn_gap: {scope}: {hours} h {minutes} min isn't covered by any period and is billed at 0.
settings.tariff.writeback_off: Set COST_WRITE_BACK=true in .env to save costs to the database for Grafana.
settings.tariff.writeback_on: Write-back on: costs are saved to the database and show in Grafana.

settings.token.heading: Tesla API token (for vehicle controls)
settings.token.placeholder: Leave blank to use sign-in token
settings.units_note: Language and units are independent. Switching language changes only the default units; units you set by hand stay.
setup.lede: One-time setup. Then everything runs on its own.
setup.privacy: Tokens are stored encrypted on this machine and only ever sent to Tesla.
setup.step1_note: Tesla no longer lets third-party apps sign in with email and password. This helper opens Tesla's own sign-in page and gives you two tokens; your password goes only to Tesla.
setup.title: Connect your Tesla
setup.waiting_vehicle: Connected. Waiting for your vehicle to report in, usually a minute or two, or once it wakes.
timeline.sleep_note: The car actually slept for {pct}% of the time it could have. The other {idle} it was awake with nothing to do — that time costs range for nothing. The denominator counts asleep plus awake-and-idle only; offline is excluded, because a car with no signal is neither.
timeline.truncated: Showing the most recent {shown} of {total}. Narrow the range to see earlier ones.
token.src_db_down: Database unavailable — it may still be starting
token.src_env: Using the token from the environment
trips.not_in_range: That drive is not in the most recent {n}; showing the latest instead.
trips.pick_hint: Select a trip to see its route
usb.drop.hint: Plug the USB drive into this computer, then pick the TeslaCam folder or the whole drive, or drag it in.
usb.drop.privacy: Nothing is uploaded: clips and driving data are processed in your browser. Only clips you import go to the hub, for exports and data overlays.
usb.empty: No TeslaCam clips found. Pick the drive's root or the TeslaCam folder.
usb.hevc: Won't play? HEVC needs hardware decoding in the browser; try Safari or Edge, or import the clip and export it as H.264.
usb.import.desc: Imported clips can be exported as MP4 with battery, power and elevation overlays, and kept long term.
